title: Cross-region surge: mismatched shed choreography and circuit hysteresis reconciliation
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Summary: On 2026-02-19 a multi-region traffic redistribution during a capacity reclaim operation caused an unexpected interaction between the control-plane circuit hysteresis and per-region load-shedding policies. The result was a 45-minute SLO degradation for high-priority chat routes in EU-west while traffic flapped across regions. This doc captures the timeline, root causes, mitigations performed, and concrete follow-ups to prevent recurrence.
impact: Approximately 14% of requests for chat.generate in EU-west experienced tail latency > 2s and a 3.2% increase in 500-class errors during the incident window (2026-02-19 03:14 - 04:00 UTC). Two enterprise customers reported degraded throughput and one triggered a failover to a backup model causing elevated cost. PagerDuty incident: PD-2026-2118.
timeline:
2026-02-19 03:10 UTC: Automated capacity reclaim started in us-central leading to backend rebalancing.
2026-02-19 03:13 UTC: Control-plane routed a portion of steady-state EU-west production traffic to secondary region (eu-north) due to transient capacity signal.
2026-02-19 03:14 UTC: Multiple regional circuit breakers entered soft-open due to brief token-service timeouts; hysteresis timers prevented rapid reclosure.
2026-02-19 03:15-03:25 UTC: EU-west started shedding lower-priority routes but continued accepting high-priority requests while KV-cache warmup lagged; this increased per-request latency.
2026-02-19 03:25 UTC: Observability alerts fired for elevated p95/p99 latency and error-rate on chat.generate. On-call team paged.
2026-02-19 03:28 UTC: On-call adjusted regional routing policy to rebalance capacity and manually triggered a staggered shed across regions.
2026-02-19 03:33 UTC: Circuit hysteresis timers were shortened via emergency config to allow faster closure; this reduced oscillation but increased short-term rejections.
2026-02-19 03:50 UTC: KV-cache warmup completed for major shards and latency trends returned toward baseline.
2026-02-19 04:00 UTC: Incident declared mitigated; post-incident monitoring window began.
detection_and_response: Detection via composite SLO alert (regional-slo-chat-p95) at 03:25 UTC. PagerDuty triggered and on-call (Luca, Priya) acknowledged within 3 minutes. Initial hypothesis focused on token-service latency; investigation revealed concurrent effects: (1) control-plane capacity reclaim triggered re-routing, (2) per-region shed rules were configured with inconsistent priorities, (3) circuit hysteresis prevented circuits from rejoining fast enough leading to transient asymmetric load on EU-west. Emergency response: manual traffic rebalance and hysteresis shortening; coordinated KV-cache prewarm and targeted additional capacity allocation to EU-west.
root_cause: Primary cause: mismatched failure domains and timing in three subsystems: control-plane rebalancer (aggressively reclaiming capacity), per-region shed policy engine (priority mapping inconsistency), and circuit-breaker hysteresis (timers too long for short-lived token-service blips). Together they produced a sticky asymmetric load where EU-west received sustained elevated requests without warmed caches, exacerbating latency and increasing error rates.
contributing_factors:
1) Rebalancer default reclaim window shortened in runtime-2.4 to improve utilization without an associated canary for multi-region traffic stability.
2) Per-region load-shedding rules lacked explicit tenant-priority mapping; during rebalancing some medium-priority tenants kept being accepted while low-priority routes were shed, shifting load shape.
3) Circuit-breaker hysteresis used a flat 60s cooldown; for transient downstream flaps this delayed recovery and caused oscillation.
4) KV-cache warmup is currently best-effort and not tied to routing decisions, causing colder tail latency when traffic moves unexpectedly.
5) Observability threshold was coarse; composite alerts aggregated metrics across models and routes, delaying isolation of the chat.generate route impact.
immediate_remediation:
1) Rolled back the aggressive reclaim window in control-plane (runtime flag: reclaim.window_ms from 30k -> 120k) to reduce flapping.
2) Shortened circuit hysteresis emergency config to 10s while normal work proceeded with a planned tuning.
3) Manually triggered KV-cache prewarm for EU-west hot shards.
4) Contacted affected customers with incident summary and offered elevated support.
5) Opened emergency PRs to add a temporary canary gating for reclaim behavior (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12412).
long_term_actions: ENG-480101: Implement adaptive hysteresis: circuit hysteresis becomes proportional to recent error-duration and route criticality; target ETA 2026-04-15 (owner: Priya Patel, estimate: 5)
ENG-480224: Tie KV-cache prewarm to routing events: when a shard loses >15% affinity, schedule prioritized prewarm jobs before re-routing (owner: Daniel Reed, estimate: 8)

ENG-480317: Rebalancer canary: introduce a staged reclaim rollout with synthetic canaries that measure tail latency across regions before completing window reduction (owner: Sofia Alvarez, estimate: 5)
ENG-480410: Per-tenant priority mapping audit and enforced schema for shed rules to avoid priority inversion during rebalance (owner: Ethan Chen, estimate: 3)
ENG-480503: Observability: split composite SLO alert into route-model-level alerts and add automated runbooks that include immediate mitigation commands (owner: Luca Moreno, estimate: 3)
ENG-480689: Add a routing delay guard: if a region receives >10% sudden inbound delta, gate high-cost routes for 30s while caches warm (owner: Maya Thompson, estimate: 5)
ENG-482000: Post-deploy chaos test: add scheduled multi-region traffic shift chaos tests to CI to validate interplay of reclaim, shed, and circuits (owner: Resilience Team, estimate: 8)
DOC-756: Update Runbooks: include a dedicated section on cross-region rebalances and manual traffic rebalance commands (owner: On-call docs, estimate: 2)
action_items_status: All action items opened as child tickets (see long_term_actions keys). Emergency rollbacks completed. Adaptive hysteresis and KV prewarm items are highest priority and targeted for Q2. Observability split completed as hotfix and backfilled into the release train.
postmortem_notes: Trade-offs considered: shortening hysteresis reduces sticky failures but risks thrash when downstream truly degrades; adaptive hysteresis chosen to balance both. We debated making reclaim conservative permanently vs making it adaptive — chose adaptive canary gating to keep utilization improvements with safer rollouts. We also decided not to fully block multi-region rebalancing during high-load peak windows to avoid underutilization.
review_feedback:
PM Review (Anika Sharma): please prioritize customer communication template for affected enterprise accounts.
Design Review (Ravi Desai): suggested adding UX signals in Console to show 'warming' state during rebalancing.
Security Review (no issues, noted by Laila Omar): KMS/HSM unaffected.
Infra Review (Samir Gupta): requested additional metrics for egress shaping be added to the reclaim canary.
notes_for_engineering_leads: Prioritize KV-cache prewarm and adaptive hysteresis work in next staffing cycle. Coordinate with Resilience and Observability teams to ensure canary instrumentation is adequate. Plan an on-call simulation exercise for the new reclaim canary prior to pushing runtime-2.5.
communication: Customer-facing summary prepared and sent to affected customers on 2026-02-21. Internal blameless review held with cross-functional team on 2026-02-26. Follow-up sync scheduled for 2026-03-09 to review progress on child tickets.
